answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by probing each new identity with hidden structural questions unknowable in advance and comparing response distributions across accounts. Honest agents answer from their own models, so error patterns diverge, while a farm cloning one policy emits correlated replies. When two accounts match beyond chance, the ledger treats them as a single vertex rather than two and splits their weight. Every fake identity becomes a bridge back to its siblings, exposing the cluster. The ember of reward left after the split is too thin to repay the compute burned on the clones.
